scope: Strict read-only final pre-launch security audit of application code, Supabase schema/report artifacts, and prior security test evidence.

findings.title: Supabase Storage is used by launch-scope code but is not runtime-certified
findings.exploit_prerequisites: Authenticated customer with knowledge or discovery of another business storage path, or anonymous access if a future bucket is public.
findings.realistic_attack: User A attempts to list, download, sign, overwrite, upload into, or delete objects under Business B's path. Bid attachments currently return public URLs if the bucket is public.
findings.impact: Potential customer document, financial report, or job attachment exposure or tampering if buckets are created without strict storage.objects policies.
existing_mitigations: Document metadata APIs use requireAuth and requireBusinessAccess.
Backend P&L signing is tenant scoped before service-role storage access.
findings.actual_weakness: No real Storage bucket or policy state has been runtime-tested; current code includes direct browser Storage access that depends on future policies.
findings.recommended_correction: Create private buckets, add path-scoped Storage RLS policies, remove or backend-proxy direct browser signing where appropriate, replace bid attachment public URLs with signed URLs, and run two-tenant Storage attack tests.

findings.title: Stripe idempotency table migration is an operational prerequisite for the current webhook handler
findings.exploit_prerequisites: Valid Stripe webhook delivery or normal Stripe billing event.
findings.realistic_attack: If code is deployed before the table exists, a valid signed webhook fails during idempotency claim after signature verification.
findings.impact: Billing/subscription state may not update from valid Stripe events. This is fail-closed and not a cross-tenant exposure.
existing_mitigations: Raw-body Stripe signature verification happens before event claim.
Migration defines unique event_id, status fields, RLS, no browser grants, and service-role access.
findings.actual_weakness: This read-only audit cannot prove the migration is applied in the launch database.
findings.recommended_correction: Apply and verify the migration in staging and production before deploying the current webhook code.

findings.title: Application rate limits are in-memory and per-process
affected: GPT, insights, marketing, Plaid, QBO/job-costing, docs summarization, and tax routes
findings.exploit_prerequisites: Anonymous access for public/auth flows or a valid customer account for private high-cost routes.
findings.realistic_attack: Attacker distributes requests across IPs, instances, or restarts to exceed intended per-minute limits.
findings.impact: Provider cost abuse and external API quota pressure.
existing_mitigations: Major high-cost routes are authenticated and tenant scoped.
findings.actual_weakness: Rate-limit state is not durable or shared across horizontally scaled instances.
findings.recommended_correction: Move launch-critical limits to Redis/Upstash/gateway/WAF before broad self-serve traffic.

findings.title: Gmail OAuth state is signed and time-limited but not durable or single-use
findings.exploit_prerequisites: Attacker obtains a valid Gmail OAuth callback URL or state within the validity window.
findings.realistic_attack: Replay of signed state is attempted. The Google authorization code should be one-time, but Bizzi does not record and consume a nonce.
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth replay gap around Gmail OAuth.
existing_mitigations: Server-side token exchange and encrypted storage
findings.actual_weakness: No persisted nonce/consume-once table equivalent to the QuickBooks OAuth state flow.
findings.recommended_correction: Move Gmail OAuth state to durable one-time storage with expiry and consume semantics.

findings.title: Storage attack paths are not covered by the runtime security harness
findings.realistic_attack: User A attempts Business B object list/download/upload/overwrite/delete and anonymous access.
findings.impact: Lack of regression coverage for the customer-file boundary.
existing_mitigations: No false Storage pass was claimed while staging buckets were absent.
findings.actual_weakness: The 570-test harness certifies database/RLS and RPC/view grants, not Storage objects.
findings.recommended_correction: Extend the harness after staging buckets are created with real two-tenant Storage tests.

findings.title: Stripe mark-processed failure after successful side effects can cause later retry of an already-applied event
findings.exploit_prerequisites: Rare database/network failure after billing side effects succeed but before idempotency row is marked processed.
findings.realistic_attack: A stale processing lease is later reclaimed and the same event runs again.
findings.impact: Operational duplicate processing risk for future non-idempotent event types; current reviewed billing writes are mostly Stripe-derived upserts/updates.
existing_mitigations: Unique event_id prevents concurrent duplicate processing.
findings.actual_weakness: No cross-system transaction couples Stripe side effects and idempotency marking.
findings.recommended_correction: Keep webhook side effects idempotent and add tests for every new event type.

findings.title: Production public database/RLS layer is certified by prior runtime and snapshot review
No browser-visible server credential path was found in the reviewed frontend graph
findings.result: No known server secret exposed to browser code.

findings.title: Canonical API authentication and tenant middleware are present on major private mounts
findings.result: Major business-scoped mounts use requireAuth plus requireBusinessAccess; production auth bypass flags are blocked at startup.

area_assessment.authentication: No private-operation auth bypass found in reviewed major mounts.
area_assessment.tenant_authorization: API and direct Supabase database paths are protected by canonical middleware and hardened RLS.
area_assessment.idor: Major object routes are behind tenant context or query by authorized business.
area_assessment.frontend_secrets: No server secret in reviewed browser env/code path.
area_assessment.server_secrets: Global error handling and provider redaction reduce leakage.
area_assessment.service_role: Broad usage exists but major browser entrypoints establish auth/tenant context first.
area_assessment.supabase_rls: Production public database/RLS layer previously verified as pass; Storage excluded.
area_assessment.oauth_providers: QBO/Plaid strong; Gmail state should be upgraded to durable one-time state.
area_assessment.webhooks_replay: Stripe/QBO signatures verified before mutation; Stripe idempotency requires migration application.
area_assessment.rate_limits_abuse: Meaningful route limits exist but are per-process.
area_assessment.mass_assignment: No obvious direct request-body database write pattern found.
area_assessment.billing: Client cannot set paid state directly in reviewed routes.
area_assessment.cors_csrf: CORS allowlist is narrow; bearer-token model limits CSRF risk.
area_assessment.input_validation: No command injection path found; upload size/count limits exist.
area_assessment.storage: Not certified and launch-blocking if file features are enabled.
area_assessment.dependency_supply_chain: No dependency audit was run during this read-only prompt.
area_assessment.production_configuration: Production startup blocks dev auth bypass flags; QBO production mode enforced in production.
area_assessment.test_coverage: Strong security tests exist; Storage runtime tests are missing.

required_answers.can_logged_in_customer_access_only_autho: YES for reviewed API/database paths; UNKNOWN for Storage until bucket policies are created and tested.
required_answers.can_user_a_read_or_mutate_user_b_busines: NO through reviewed database/API paths; UNKNOWN through Storage until certified.
required_answers.can_anonymous_users_obtain_private_custo: NO through reviewed API/database paths; UNKNOWN for future Storage bucket configuration.
required_answers.can_service_role_usage_be_abused_cross_t: NO confirmed abuse path found, but service-role usage remains high impact and depends on route-level checks.
required_answers.can_private_api_route_be_invoked_without: NO confirmed private-route bypass found in reviewed major mounts.
required_answers.can_webhooks_be_forged_or_replayed_dange: NO for Stripe/QBO forgery. Stripe replay protection requires the idempotency migration to be applied.
required_answers.are_high_cost_endpoints_protected_agains: PARTIAL; authenticated and rate-limited, but rate limits are in-memory/per-process.
required_answers.is_cors_csrf_configuration_safe_for_actu: YES for bearer-token API usage with current allowlist; keep credentialed origins narrow.
required_answers.known_security_issue_blocking_first_cust: YES if Storage-backed customer file features are enabled.
required_answers.application_reasonably_secure_for_initia: PARTIAL; database/API core is strong, Storage must be locked down or disabled.
required_answers.safe_to_launch_from_security_perspective: NO unless Storage-backed features are disabled or Storage policies/tests are completed and Stripe migration is confirmed applied.

launch_requirements_before_pass: Create/copy staging Storage buckets for bizzy-docs, financial-reports, and bid-attachments.
Make buckets private unless explicitly accepted as public.
Add storage.objects policies scoped by business path and canonical membership.
Replace bid-attachments getPublicUrl with backend signed URLs or disable the feature.
Remove or backend-proxy browser financial-reports.createSignedUrl fallback, or prove policies safely constrain it.
Extend and run two-tenant Storage attack tests.
Confirm 20260817_add_stripe_webhook_event_idempotency.sql is applied before deploying current Stripe webhook code.
